Definition: of Chaldee origin (compare H4026); the tower; Magdala (i.e. Migdala), a place in Palestine:--Magdala.
BiblicalUsage: Magdala was a place on the shore of Galilee, and it appears once, in Matthew 15:39, where Jesus sent the multitudes away and came into the coasts of Magdala after feeding the four thousand. The Greek text spells the place with a different ending from the form Strong's lists, which is why the indexes carry it under that spelling.
TheologicalSignificance: I take it that Magdala matters because of who came from there: the town gave its name to Mary Magdalene.
